cells.tense: You are in the private testing now and the commitment is holding under it.
cells.ask: Tell one person what the last hard stretch cost you and what it kept. No fixing, no summary. Just the account, out loud, to someone who'll let it stand.
cells.core:
The private work is paying off. You've been through enough friction with your own commitments to know which ones hold and which were habit, and that knowing shows up in how you sit with people — you don't flinch when someone brings you something heavy. The connection runs without you forcing it, and the care isn't draining you.

What this balance is free to feed next is the pace of it. You can keep tending the people in front of you, and you can also let some of that tending land on what you've built. There's a difference between holding space and clutching, and you can feel it right now. The ask is to tell one person what the last hard stretch cost you and what it kept — plainly, without fixing anything or summing it up. Someone who lets your account stand.
cells.sheetLine: Your commitments have been tested and the care still runs clean.
cells.verb: testing what you're actually committed to through friction, behind closed doors
cells.place: the room where you feel with people and hold your own ground

cells.tense: You are bracing for a test that hasn't arrived and rehearsing it with the people close to you.
cells.ask: Pick one relationship and let a whole week pass without checking where it stands. If you catch yourself making contact to check, note what it was for and let the note sit.
cells.core:
You're running the private test ahead of the people in it. There's a version ahead where your commitment has been proved and you're already living there — so conversations get checked for signs, silences get read, and the people close to you meet the rehearsal instead of you.

Feeling with someone doesn't survive that much verifying. What's underneath is a real question about what you're committed to, and scanning other people for evidence won't answer it. The ask is to pick one relationship and let a whole week pass without checking where it stands. If you catch yourself making contact to check, note what it was for and let the note sit. What you're testing for isn't out there to find.
cells.sheetLine: You're testing them for an answer that's yours to find.

cells.tense: You stopped bringing yourself into the room and the room went on without you.
cells.ask: In one conversation this week, say the thing you actually think before checking whether it fits. One sentence. Let it land however it lands and stay in the room.
cells.core:
You used to be in the room with people and now you're at the edge of it. Nobody's complaining. You're present enough to pass, kind enough to be counted, and not actually in it. The absence is quiet and it's been going on long enough that it feels like your temperament.

The missing piece isn't feeling. It's the willingness to be changed by someone again, which is what connection costs. The ask is small: in one conversation this week, say the thing you actually think before checking whether it fits. One sentence. Let it land however it lands and stay in the room after it. Strength is already moving your way from the people around you; you only have to let it arrive.

cells.tense: You are already moved by the people around you and you keep calling it good manners.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did this week out of care for someone and had been filing under logistics. Say it plainly, once, without making it smaller.
cells.core:
You feel with people — it shapes what you do, the words you pick, what you notice and let pass. You'd describe it as being practical, or just doing your part, or not making a thing of it. Meanwhile the connection is already running and doing real work, and the only one giving it no credit is you.

What's been happening isn't a mystery. Something real has been growing between you and the people you're close to, and you haven't claimed it as yours. Growth that doesn't force itself doesn't need an announcement — it needs an owner. The ask is to name one thing you did this week out of care and had been filing under logistics. Say it plainly, once, without making it smaller.
cells.sheetLine: The care is already yours. You've been calling it logistics.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person is already feeling with others and calling it something else — the record gives the capacity, not its presence in any particular day. A reader could reasonably say 'no, I know exactly what I'm doing when I sit with someone,' and the cell should still leave them something. The ask survives being wrong because it only asks to name what's already there, not to manufacture feeling. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'your tenderness is already working' — it flatters the reader's eye and I've kept it out of the cores.
